On a rainy Sunday, I had the pleasure of visiting **Café Colony**, a charming Irani café located in Hindu Colony, Dadar. The weather itself was perfect for the experience, as the comforting aroma of freshly brewed tea and baked bread created a warm, nostalgic atmosphere. The café has that classic Irani charm, with its simple yet inviting interiors that make you feel at home the moment you step in.

I began with their famous **Irani chai and brun maska**, and it was everything I had hoped for. The chai was strong, perfectly balanced with milk and sugar, and paired beautifully with the soft-yet-crispy brun generously slathered with butter. It was the kind of combination that instantly lifts your mood on a rainy day. Next, I tried the **keema fry with pav**, which turned out to be another highlight of the visit. The keema was spiced just right—rich, hearty, and bursting with authentic flavor—while the pav was fresh and fluffy, making it a wholesome and satisfying dish.

To end the meal on a sweet note, I indulged in their famous **gaz sweet**, a delicacy that lived up to its reputation. Its unique taste and texture added a perfect finishing touch to the experience, leaving me with a lasting impression of the café’s culinary heritage.

What made the visit even more special was the interaction with the lady owner of Café Colony. She was warm, courteous, and genuinely interested in knowing how we enjoyed the food. During our conversation, I shared that I am from Delhi and thoroughly enjoyed experiencing these authentic Irani dishes in Mumbai. Her hospitality, combined with the food, made the outing truly memorable.

Overall, Café Colony is not just about food—it’s about warmth, tradition, and conversations. A must-visit gem in Dadar.

featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Trofima, Shivaji Park, Dadar, Mumbai

Cafe Trofima, located near the bustling Shivaji Park in Dadar, has garnered attention as a popular hangout spot, but it falls short of the hype for several reasons.

Food

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. While it has some redeeming qualities like decent seating and satisfactory service, the compromised food taste, lack of parking, and high prices make it hard to recommend wholeheartedly. It could work as a one-time visit for those curious about its breakfast platters, but better options are available in and around the area for a more satisfying experience.

Overall Rating: 2/5

featured_reviews.review_text:
Great Spot for an Unbeatable Cup of Chai and Quick Munchies

If you're looking for a solid place to grab a classic cutting chai or a quick evening snack in Parel, Chaos Control Cafe is a fantastic choice. Located right in the thick of the action, this spot has become immensely famous among the younger crowd, college students, and office folks looking to unwind. The vibe here is always energetic and buzzing.
The absolute star of the show here is their tea. They serve an amazing, deeply flavorful Kolkata-style chai in traditional clay kulhads that hits the spot every single time. Paired with their unique snack options like the Varanasi Toast or Bun Maska, it makes for a perfect, pocket-friendly evening ritual. However, a quick word of advice: if you are a hard-core coffee lover, this might not be the place for you. Their coffee simply doesn't match up to the brilliant standards of their chai, so it's best to stick to the tea menu.
As for the ambiance, it's a very small outlet, so indoor sitting is highly limited. In true Mumbai fashion, they have cleverly converted the adjacent side street into an open-air sitting area. It is a prime example of a typical, resourceful Mumbai jugad—sitting under the open sky amidst the city's chaotic energy. While it might not offer a premium, air-conditioned cafe experience, it completely works for a casual hangout with friends.
Overall, for a great cup of tea, tasty quick bites, and a lively neighbourhood atmosphere, it's highly recommended. Just skip the coffee and enjoy the street-side vibe!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointing Experience at Coffee By Di Bella, Dadar Shivaji Park

As a devoted fan of Coffee By Di Bella, I was excited to visit their Dadar Shivaji Park outlet. However, my recent experience left me disappointed and unable to recommend this particular branch.

Firstly, the ambience was quite dull, with poor lighting that didn't create a pleasant atmosphere. On the positive side, the service was prompt and efficient, which was a relief.

When it came to the food, there were mixed results. I decided to try the spinach and corn cheese sandwich, but unfortunately, it didn't live up to my expectations. The taste was underwhelming, and I felt it could have been better. On the other hand, the Nutella Waffle was truly amazing, and I highly recommend it to anyone with a sweet tooth.

However, what frustrated me the most was the handling of our order for a mojito. Initially, they took our order, but after waiting for 30 minutes, they informed us that they had run out of mint and couldn't deliver it. It would have been much better if they had informed us right away instead of making us wait. They then asked for an additional 30 minutes to arrange the mint, which I found quite irritating.

Overall, my experience at Coffee By Di Bella, Dadar Shivaji Park, was not up to par. While the coffee was good and the service was satisfactory, the dull ambience, disappointing sandwich, and mishandling of our order left a sour taste in my mouth. I'm sorry to say that I cannot recommend this particular outlet.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Modern Coffee Haven Beside Historic Grounds, this Starbucks branch captures that classic blend of convenience, comfort, and quality coffee in bustling Dadar West.

Inside, the space is small yet well-kept, offering cozy seating, good lighting, and occasional views of the leafy park through open walls—a pleasant mix of café buzz and outdoor serenity . It’s popular with both friends hanging out and solo visitors catching up on work or simply enjoying some downtime. Many visitors find it approachable and cozy, with staff delivering courteous service,

On my visit, I ordered a Caramel Macchiato and a Blueberry Muffin, The drink had a standard Starbucks profile—smooth espresso layered with steamed milk and caramel—but felt slightly weaker than expected, lacking richer caramel notes, which aligns with some other customer feedback. The muffin was fresh and pleasantly moist, though not overly sweet—a decent snack to pair with the beverage.

The cafe earns ratings around 4.4 out of 5 on official listings and about 4.5 based on hundreds of reviews—reflecting generally high satisfaction in atmosphere and service, though Zomato lists a more moderate 3.2 dining rating- suggesting some variability in customer experience .

For me, the service was attentive,the staff helpful, and they even engage in ad‑hoc coffee tastings and discussions about the beans—something that felt both informative and welcoming.
In short,this Starbucks outlet is a solid choice for anyone looking to unwind near Shivaji Park—offering good coffee, clean ambience, and friendly service. If you prize boldness in flavor, you might occasionally find the espresso a touch mild—but overall, a comfortable, reliable café experience in Dadar West.

featured_reviews.name: Nirav Gangar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The overall ambience of the restaurant looked amazing when we entered and we were very excited about having lunch at the restaurant, but were extremely disappointed as and when each food item came from our orders.
Below are the items we ordered for -
1. Broccoli almond soup - It tasted as if we were having a canned soup. Did not like the taste at all.
2. Sweet corn soup - A canned sweet corn soup was simply heated and presented to us in a bowl. Definitely not recommended. You can definitely avoid having soups here!
3. Honey chilli potato - It was very very sweet. It seemed only honey was added and no chilli mixed.
4. Paneer hunan style - It was good. Liked it.
5. Corn cheese balls - The balls were very very dry. Did not enjoy at all.
6. Sanj saveera - It was very okay. Can avoid. Try some other vegetable.
7. Veg dewani handi - It was good. Liked it better than the other vegetable.
8. Indian breads - tandoori garlic roti, butter fulka, tandoori roti, butter garlic kulcha - all the breads were very well made. Had asked for the kulcha to be extra crispy and it was made as per request.
9. Veg Thai curry - This curry was probably the best part of the meal! Absolutely enjoyed it! Must try.
10.  Butter garlic rice - The rice was very well made. Enjoyed it with the curry.
11. Fresh lime soda - on a holiday there was no staff available for the mocktails so only drinks like fresh lime were available. It was decent.

All in all, there is a lot of room for improvement. Especially in the soups and starters. Wouldn’t recommend going here until some major changes are made in the kitchen.
